name: HUNTER
summary: HUNTER is a laboratory-scale proposal for keV sterile-neutrino searches using laser-cooled radioactive atoms. It reconstructs missing neutrino mass from the complete visible products of electron capture.
detection_principle: 131Cs atoms are held in a magneto-optical trap. X rays, recoil ions and Auger electrons are measured in coincidence, permitting energy-momentum reconstruction. A massive-neutrino component would appear in the missing-mass distribution.

status.evidence: The design and white paper describe a staged search and forecast sensitivity; they do not establish a completed sterile-neutrino discovery experiment.

key_parameters.value: 131Xe recoil ion, X rays and Auger electrons

results.summary: Presented an apparatus design and forecast sensitivity, rather than a measured exclusion.

science_scope: A sterile state is sought through missing kinematics in nuclear decay. Forecast sensitivity depends on source statistics and detector resolution; the apparatus drawing does not imply an observation.
